sources.title: Philippine Registry of Cultural Property (NCCA): Naga City entries
sources.note: Inspected October 9, 2026. Naga Station (Himpilan ng Naga): Work of National Artist for Architecture Pablo S. Antonio, citing The Architectural Legacy of Pablo S. Antonio: 1901-1975. The registry listing is the basis for this landmark's Heritage legend membership. Street View (October 2024) shows the rebuilt station without Antonio's river-stone walls, so no construction year is set.

text.en: Naga station opened on April 1, 1920, on the Manila Railroad Company's Legazpi Division line.
By 1938, the Legazpi Division had merged into the Main Line South.
The national registry lists the station among the works of National Artist for Architecture Pablo S. Antonio, whose terminals were built of large stacked river stones.
The present station building was rebuilt and opened in 2009.
